exposure: Design and implementation of the PowerMom digital health platform
Digital recruitment strategies (digital advertisements, pregnancy apps, consortium)
Multimodal data collection (self-reported surveys, wearable devices, electronic health records)
outcome: Participant engagement metrics (survey completion rates, wearable device data sharing, EHR connection)
Lessons learned for future digital maternal health studies
cohort: The cohort consists of 5617 pregnant and postpartum individuals recruited from 2021 to 2024 via digital advertisements, pregnancy apps, and a consortium of organizations across all 50 US states, Puerto Rico, and Guam.
finding: The PowerMom platform successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using digital tools to recruit and engage diverse populations in maternal health research and integrate multimodal data sources, despite challenges with data completeness and survey attrition.
